judgment.rationale: Both Skills share the resolved Grade 3 coordinate (rank 3) and the identity scope Grade 3 | Term 3 | Reading and Phonics | Group Guided Reading, appearing as separate bullets in the same printed table cell (row=3, window 49, page 123). Same-rank, same-Term buildsTowards requires substantive extension evidence, which is absent, so the symmetric relatesTo with null direction is the supported judgment. judgment.rationale: Both SFIs are Grade 1, Term 1 Skills, so same-rank/same-term direction is permitted only on substantive evidence. The second SFI (Reading and Phonics / Phonics sub-strand) is oral phonemic awareness: blending c-a-t into cat, segmenting cat into c-a-t, and consonant/vowel substitution word play, with LCs tagged blending, segmenting, phonemic awareness, sounds. The first SFI (Writing / Shared, Group and Independent Writing) is 'Writes words using letter sounds learnt', i.e. encoding words by applying letter-sound knowledge (LC tags: letter sounds, phonics, words, writing). Oral segmenting of a spoken word into its constituent phonemes and manipulating those phonemes is the enabling capability for representing those sounds with letters when writing words, so proficiency in the phonemic awareness skill supports success in the written-encoding skill; the reverse (writing supporting oral awareness) is not the curricular dependency here. This is a cross-skill-area complementary dependency within Term 1, not mere repeated wording (lexical overlap is only 'sounds'/'words'). Evidence limitation: source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so only the bounded excerpts and LCs were judged.

It does, however, give real conceptual coherence: both are Grade R oral, song-based language activities, and the Term 1 song repertoire meaningfully reinforces the song-and-rhyme material used for the Term 2 phonological awareness work. Symmetric relatesTo with null direction is therefore the correct complete judgment. judgment.rationale: The first SFI is a Grade R, Term 4 Emergent Writing / Emergent Handwriting statement ('Forms letters using finger paint, paint brushes, wax crayons'), a gross/fine-motor letter-formation activity tagged handwriting, finger paint, crayons, letters. The second is a Grade 1, Term 3 Reading and Phonics / Phonics statement ('Identifies letter-sound relationships of all single letters'), tagged letter-sound, phonics, single letters. They cohere substantively as complementary strands of alphabet knowledge: physically forming letter shapes in Grade R familiarises learners with the same letter symbols whose sounds are mapped in Grade 1 phonics. However, the evidence shows different Skill Areas (Emergent Writing vs Reading and Phonics) and different cognitive demands (motor letter formation vs grapheme-phoneme correspondence), with the only lexical overlap being the token 'letters'; that is not enough to assert that proficiency in art-media letter formation supports success in letter-sound identification, so a developmental buildsTowards is not warranted. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all nodes carry upstream audit/merge context, which limits but does not contradict this reading.

Lexical overlap is limited to function words ('and', 'the') and page proximity is weak, so no developmental direction is asserted within the same Grade R Term 4.
